title: How Buffett built wealth: Graham's value investing, Berkshire, and loving the job
summary: Buffett recounts his path from pinball machines to Ben Graham's partnership, the Buffett Partnership and Berkshire. He explains investing as assigning yourself the right story about what a business is worth, buying decent businesses at sensible prices, and why time and finding work you love matter more than money.

principles.text: Investing is valuing a business: write the story of what it is worth, then compare it to the price.
principles.quote: Investing is just about assigning yourself the right story.

principles.text: Buy decent businesses at sensible prices and back good people to run them.
principles.quote: We bought businesses that we thought were decent businesses at sensible prices and we had good people to run them.

principles.text: When fear drives a price far below intrinsic value, the gap is the opportunity.
principles.quote: So the Washington Post company, which was intrinsically worth $400 or $500 million, was selling for about 80 million in the market.

principles.text: Stay inside your circle of competence: only value what you can write the story on.
principles.quote: If you ask me to write a story on, you know, what is some glamorous but nonprofit making business worth, I don't know how to write that story.

principles.text: Screen deals quickly and say no fast; most fail simple filters.
principles.quote: I can usually tell within two or three minutes whether a deal is likely to happen or not.

principles.text: Time is the scarce resource, not money. Find work you would do for free.
principles.quote: I think you should look for the job that you would want to hold if you didn't need a job.
